linkedin:
I have three browsers and four Chrome profiles, and for years every link I clicked opened in the wrong one.

So I built TrafficControl, a small macOS menu bar app that becomes your default browser and decides where each link should go:

→ Linear, Notion, Figma, Zoom and Spotify links open in their desktop apps
→ a page you already have open brings that tab forward
→ your rules send work links to the work profile
→ anything else shows a picker right at your cursor

It's free and open source. For the next few weeks I'll post one feature a week.

alt: TrafficControl card: 'Set it once. Never think about it again.' Four rule strips: github.com/acme to Chrome Work, github.com/you to Chrome Personal, any link from Slack to Chrome Work, Command-click anywhere to Safari.
linkedin:
The rule I use most: github.com/buffer goes to my work profile, github.com/hakubo goes to my personal one. Same domain, different browser, decided by the path.

TrafficControl rules can look at:
• the domain and path
• the full URL
• the app you clicked in (everything from Slack → work)
• keys you held (⌘-click → Safari)

Match with is, contains, wildcards or regex. Rules run top to bottom, the first match wins, and a live tester shows which rule a URL would hit before you save.

linkedin:
How many copies of the same Google Doc do you have open right now?

Before TrafficControl opens a link, it checks your running browsers for a tab that already shows that page. If there is one, it brings that tab forward instead of opening another.

It doesn't care about http vs https, www., a trailing slash, the #anchor or tracking parameters like utm_source, so the link from the newsletter matches the tab you already have.

Works with Safari, Chrome, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi and Chromium. macOS asks once per browser for permission.

linkedin:
Nobody wants to sit down and write browser rules. So TrafficControl learns them from you.

Hold ⌘ while you pick a browser and that choice becomes the rule for the site. The picker shows a pin and tells you exactly what it will save.

It also keeps a short history of the domains you open and where they went. Next time, your usual choice is already selected, and Settings → History turns any domain into a rule with one click.

The history is a JSON file on your Mac. It never leaves it, and you can switch it off.

linkedin:
What happens between clicking a link and seeing the page? With TrafficControl, five checks, in this order:

1. Desktop app: is it a Linear, Notion, Figma, Zoom or Spotify link, and is the app running?
2. Open tab: is the page already open somewhere?
3. Your rules: first match wins
4. Default: your primary browser, the only one running, or the last one you used
5. Picker: anything left appears at your cursor

Hold ⇧ while clicking to skip straight to the picker.

linkedin:
Last post in the TrafficControl series. If your links still open in the wrong browser, here's the install:

brew install --cask hakubo/tap/trafficcontrol

Or download the DMG from the site. Then click Make Default in Settings.

It's free and open source, updates itself, and needs no account. Settings and history stay on your Mac.

If you want something more powerful, Choosy is the app that inspired it. If TrafficControl saves you some tab juggling, I'd love to hear what rules you set up.
